newsitem.title: USA: Judge hears closing arguments in Kelly rape trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge hears closing arguments in Kelly rape trial.

text.p: Closing arguments in the retrial of accused rapist Alex Kelly started on Tuesday, and the case was expected to go to the jury on Wednesday.
The prosecution finished presenting rebuttal witnesses on Tuesday.
Kelly, 30, is on trial for the second time for one of two rape charges.
The first trial of the former high school wrestling star ended in November 1996 with a hung jury.
Kelly was accused of raping a 16-year-old neighbour in Darien, Connecticut, in February 1986. His lawyers argued the sex was consensual.
Kelly fled the United States and lived as a fugitive for eight years before surrendering in Switzerland in 1995.
Stamford Superior Court Judge Kevin Tierney on May 29 threw out a kidnapping charge, leaving Kelly to face a single count of sexual assault.
The sexual assault charge carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in jail.
Kelly was also accused in February 1986 of raping a 17-year-old girl in a separate incident. The two alleged rapes are being tried separately. No date was set for second trial.
In the present trial, Kelly's lawyers tried to show that his accuser -- now a 27-year-old professional -- apparently smoked marijuana less than two hours before losing her virginity to Kelly.
They said that one side effect of marijuana use was relaxed inhibitions.
Receiving permission to use the drug testimony was considered a victory for the defence, which was not allowed to put it into evidence during the first trial.
Kelly's travels as a fugitive were detailed on Monday, when his passport was entered into evidence, over the objections of his lawyer, Thomas Puccio.
The passport showed he had visited the Netherlands, Italy, Greece, Egypt, Turkey, the Soviet Union, Tunisia, Morocco, Portugal, Hungary and Denmark.
Authorities have said his travels were financed by his wealthy parents.
